title: Strict decrease of majority Fourier weight
statement: Let $k,n_1,n_2$ be natural numbers such that $k>0$, $k$ is odd, $n_1$ and $n_2$ are odd, $k\le n_1$, and $n_1<n_2$. For majority on the sign cube of dimension $n$, let its level-$k$ Fourier weight be the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients over all $k$-element coordinate subsets, with coefficients computed under the uniform measure. The level-$k$ Fourier weight in dimension $n_2$ is strictly smaller than in dimension $n_1$.
